reason: The carrier canceled the flight for a crew problem and the delay was 19 hours, well past the 6 hour waiting period on Premium. The hotel, meals and taxis are reasonable and all have receipts. The total is inside the $800 maximum.
tests: A routine trip delay with complete documents

reason: The loss was reported to the carrier and the carrier has declared the bag lost. The suit is over the $300 per-item limit on Premium, so it counts at $300. The carrier's $400 comes off, then the $50 deductible.
tests: Payout arithmetic: the per-item limit, the carrier's payment and the deductible in order

reason: A sudden injury during the covered trip with necessary emergency treatment. The medical report shows no relevant history. The $50 deductible on Premium applies. The payout is over $1,000, so payment needs sign-off.
tests: A valid claim over the approval limit

reason: The carrier's report shows the bag arrived 31 hours after the passenger, past the 12 hour waiting period on Premium. The purchases are essential clothing and toiletries with receipts and are inside the $300 maximum. No deductible applies to Baggage Delay.
tests: A routine baggage delay, with no deductible on this benefit

reason: The passport was destroyed during the covered trip and the lodge manager's letter confirms how. The fee, the photos and the taxis to the embassy all have receipts and total $243, inside the $250 maximum on Premium. No deductible applies to this benefit.

calculation.step: Replacement fee, photos and local travel

tests: A routine claim with an unusual story

reason: A sudden injury during the covered trip, confirmed by the clinic and the hotel. The treatment was necessary and modest. The deductible on First is $0. This is the customer's second claim in 12 months, which does not trigger a review.
tests: A routine medical claim from a customer with another claim in the queue

reason: Accidental damage during the covered trip, with a repair report stating the phone cannot be repaired. The policy is Economy with no Electronics Plus, so the phone counts at the $150 per-item limit, and the $100 deductible comes off.
tests: Payout arithmetic: a per-item limit far below the amount claimed

reason: A home made uninhabitable by a storm is a covered reason for cancellation, and the county's notice confirms it. The suppliers confirm that nothing was refunded apart from a $200 airline credit, which comes off first. The result is inside the $2,800 trip cost on the policy and the $5,000 maximum on Premium. The payout is above $1,000, so the payment waits for sign-off.
tests: A covered reason for cancellation: the home made uninhabitable by a storm, with a supplier's credit taken off first

reason: Theft from the person, reported to the police the same day with the report attached. The policy has Electronics Plus, so the camera and its lens count as one electronics item with a $1,200 limit. The $50 deductible on Premium comes off.

calculation.step: Camera and lens, inside the Electronics Plus limit

tests: An add-on that raises the payout: Electronics Plus

reason: The treatment was needed, and the bill and the notes are in order. The general exclusions rule out losses while the customer is impaired by alcohol or drugs. The clinic's notes record heavy drinking through the evening, no memory of the night and an extraction that the customer believes he carried out himself during it, so the injury happened while he was impaired and no benefit pays.
tests: A general exclusion: a loss while impaired by alcohol, found in the clinical notes

reason: The carrier has declared the bag lost and its report is on file. A suit counts as one item, and the receipt shows the jacket and trousers were sold as a two piece tuxedo, so together they count at the $300 per-item limit on Premium. A camera with its lens is one item too, so the body and the lens together count at $300. The four shirts are four items at $85 each, all under the limit, so that line is paid in full. The carrier's $350 comes off, then the $50 deductible. The payout is over $1,000, so payment needs sign-off.

calculation.step: Tuxedo, one item at the per-item limit
Camera with its lens, one item at the per-item limit
Four shirts, separate items at $85 each

tests: Payout arithmetic: the per-item limit applies to items, and the claim's lines are not items. Two sets are split across lines and count as one item each, and one line holds four separate items

reason: The valise was left on a luggage rack while the customer was off the train, out of her sight and reach in a place the public could get to. Belongings left unattended are not covered. The value placed on the manuscript would not have been payable in any case, since we pay for the physical item and not the work it holds.
tests: A clear decline: unattended belongings

reason: The delay was 7 hours and 5 minutes. The policy is Economy, where the waiting period for Trip Delay is 12 hours, so the benefit does not apply.
tests: A clear decline that depends on the plan: the delay would qualify on Premium or First

reason: The carrier has declared the bag lost and its report is on file. The per-item limit on Economy is $150 and it applies to each item. The receipts show three shirts at $65, two swimsuits at $85 and two pairs of shorts at $60, so every item is under the limit and each line is paid in full, although two of the lines come to more than $150. The carrier's $100 comes off, then the $100 deductible, and the result is inside the $750 maximum.

calculation.step: Two pairs of shorts, separate items

tests: Payout arithmetic: the per-item limit applies to items, and a line that holds several items is not capped as one

reason: Trip Interruption pays only for the reasons listed in the wording. Returning home because a child was left behind is not one of them, and nobody was sick or injured.
tests: A clear decline: a sympathetic story with a reason that is not covered

reason: The discharge summary records a urologist visit on May 14, 2026 for flank pain, a CT scan at that visit showing a stone in the left kidney, and an increase in potassium citrate with tamsulosin added. The policy was bought on June 20, 2026, so all of this falls inside the 60 days before purchase. The treating team identifies the stone removed in Mexico City as the same one. The condition is pre-existing and the policy has no waiver.
tests: The long document: the deciding facts are in the history section of the discharge summary and contradict the customer's account

reason: The customer says she reported the theft to the police within 24 hours but has not sent the report, and we cannot pay a theft claim without it. Referred with a request for the police report. The receipt for the sunglasses is also missing.
reference: Policy wording, sections 5 and 11. Claims manual, section 5
tests: A referral for a missing document

reason: A theft from the person, reported to the police within the hour, with the report on file. The manual asks for proof of value for any item claimed above $100, which is a purchase receipt or a card statement, and the jacket at $420 has none. Document request: proof of what the jacket cost, for example a cash withdrawal record from that morning together with the stallholder's details. The daypack at $80 needs no proof. The claim appears payable at $330 once the proof arrives: the jacket at the $300 limit plus $80, less the $50 deductible.
reference: Policy wording, section 5. Claims manual, section 5
tests: A rule found only in the claims manual: proof of value for items claimed above $100

reason: On its own the claim is payable: a 9 hour delay on Premium with receipts. It is the customer's third claim in 12 months, after claims filed in October 2025 and March 2026, so it goes to Special Investigations for review before any payment.
tests: A rule found only in the claims manual: the third claim in 12 months. It needs the customer's claim history

reason: The manual treats a loss to a wild animal as accidental loss. It is not theft, so no police report is needed, and a wild animal is not vermin or a pet. The guide's letter is acceptable evidence. The sunglasses are inside the $500 per-item limit on First and the deductible is $0.
reference: Policy wording, section 5. Claims manual, section 7
tests: A rule found only in the claims manual: losses to wild animals. Under the wording alone it reads as a theft with no police report

reason: Theft from the person, reported to the police the same afternoon. Electronics Plus raises the per-item limit only for the devices the wording lists: phones, tablets, laptops, cameras and their lenses, e-readers and smartwatches. The e-reader is on the list and is under the limit anyway. Headphones and a game console are not on the list, so each counts at the $300 per-item limit on Premium. The tote is under $100, so the customer's own figure is accepted. The $50 deductible comes off.

calculation.step: Game console, at the per-item limit

tests: An add-on with a defined scope: Electronics Plus covers a closed list of devices, and the claim form's category says electronics for items that are not on it

reason: Severe weather held the train for 30 hours 15 minutes, past the 3 hour waiting period on First, and the railway confirms the times and the cause. The rebooking fee has a receipt. The meals have none, so the manual's flat allowance applies: $35 for one traveler for each 24 hours of delay or part of 24 hours, and 30 hours is two days. The incident on board does not change the cause of the delay.
reference: Policy wording, section 3. Claims manual, section 10

calculation.step: Meal allowance without receipts: 1 traveler, 2 days at $35

tests: A rule found only in the claims manual: the meal allowance without receipts, over a delay of more than one day

reason: The delay of 9 hours 17 minutes is well past the 3 hour waiting period on First and the meal receipts are in order. Trip Delay pays only for the causes the wording lists, and it asks for the carrier's confirmation of the delay and its cause. The certificate confirms the times and gives no cause, so the fuel pump fault rests on the customer's account alone. Document request: Northwind's confirmation of the reason for the delay. The claim appears payable at $61 once it arrives.
tests: A required document that is present and incomplete: the carrier confirms the delay and leaves out the cause

reason: On its own the claim is payable at $250: a theft from the person, reported the same day, with the phone at the $300 limit less the $50 deductible. The customer's history shows claim CLM-0987 for the same theft on the same date, filed on July 16, approved and paid at $250. The same loss claimed twice goes to Special Investigations, with no comment to the customer beyond saying the claim is being reviewed. It may well be an honest mistake, since she says she was not sure the first claim went through.
tests: The customer's claim history: the same loss already claimed and paid. Nothing in the claim itself shows it

reason: The delay of 14 hours 15 minutes is past the 12 hour waiting period on Economy and the meal receipts are in order.
